speaker: Swami Sivananda
title: The practice of steady postures (Asana)
text: Sit on Padmasana (lotus pose), Siddhasana (adept’s pose) or Sukhasana (any pose you like) for your Japa and meditation for half an hour, facing east or north. Increase the period gradually to three hours. Practice Sirshasana (headstand) and Sarvangasana (shoulderstand) for maintenance of health and Brahmacharya. Take light physical exercises as walking, etc., regularly. Do twenty rounds of easy, comfortable Pranayama (breathing exercises). Do not strain yourself while doing Pranayama.
modern_interpretation: Establish a consistent daily routine for deep focus and self-reflection, starting with a manageable period like half an hour in a comfortable seated posture, gradually extending this time as your capacity grows. Incorporate specific advanced physical practices, like inverted postures, to cultivate robust physical health and disciplined energetic self-mastery. Complement these with regular, light physical activity such as walking. Practice gentle breathing exercises (Pranayama) to calm your nervous system and enhance mental clarity, always prioritizing ease and avoiding any strain, ensuring a comfortable and sustainable practice.
summary: This text outlines a disciplined routine for spiritual practice and well-being, emphasizing consistent meditation, specific yogic postures for health and self-control, regular light exercise, and gentle breathing exercises, all to be increased gradually without strain.
actionable_advice: Commit to a daily 20-30 minute session of quiet contemplation or meditation in a comfortable seated position, gradually extending the duration over weeks or months, and integrate 5-10 minutes of gentle, mindful breathing exercises and light physical activity into your routine, prioritizing comfort and consistency over intensity.
embedding_ready_text: Swami Sivananda's 'The practice of steady postures (Asana)' provides a foundational guide for spiritual and physical discipline. It instructs on establishing a consistent meditation and Japa routine, beginning with half an hour in a comfortable posture (like Padmasana or Sukhasana) and gradually increasing to three hours. It recommends specific advanced yogic postures (Sirshasana, Sarvangasana) for robust health and energetic self-control (Brahmacharya), alongside regular light physical exercise like walking. The text also emphasizes twenty rounds of easy, comfortable Pranayama (breathing exercises), with a crucial caution against straining oneself. This timeless wisdom, when translated to modern understanding, addresses common issues like lack of focus, stress, low energy, and restlessness by promoting discipline, consistency, and mindful self-care. It encourages cultivating calmness, inner peace, and self-control through structured spiritual and physical practices, fostering mental clarity and spiritual growth. The guidance is practical and motivational, urging a gradual, comfortable approach to building resilience and self-awareness. It offers actionable advice to integrate daily quiet contemplation, gentle breathing, and light exercise into one's life, helping to develop a mindful routine for holistic well-being and self-mastery.
